author: charly26
text_post: is she really upset? Hi: I came back to town from a trip with my sister. It was a relaxation trip. I had told my gf we would meet the next day I get to the city, but I caught a cold which made stay home because the weather theses days is terrible. I called her on her cell and when explaining things she got upset and reminded me that I had promised her to meet after my trip. I said that I would take a rest and if I get better, we would probably meet as expected. After the connversation on the phone, I realized that we were talking about my health and that I can't risk getting worse just because I had to see my gf that day. I thought she was selfish because she just thought of herself and didn't care much about my recovery. I woke from my nap and decided to send her a message with all these ideas. She didn't repply. My sister said that my gf is annoyed because she was expecting to see me that day according to what we had planned before my trip. I think my actions about not going out to see her were ok because I was concerned about y health but it seems she doesn't understand and is still upset. I sent her a text message in the morning saying hi and wising her a nice day, she didn't answer back How to talk to her when I see her?

author: deepseadiver
text_post: Dude DO NOT apologize for anything.  You need to stick up for yourself.  She should be understanding and supportive if you are sick. Instead of explaining yourself like you did you simply just state you are not feeling well.  You reacted to he selfish diatribe giving fuel to the fire. Don't play her game, a quality girl will not act that way.  You could say "i need you to support me when I'm sick" but don't play the victim here.  Stop contacting her so much you are communicating to her that you need her more than she needs you.  You need to state your point in take it or leave it type of manner.  This is not a legitimate concern on her part.  Did she confront you directly? Don't reward bad behavior with attention.

author: charly26
text_post: We met last Saturday as planned to talk about this, so we did. There was kind of an argument because she didn't want to admit that she acted selfishly. At the end, she admitted it and apologized for that behavior. We hugged and ended making out. Problem solved. Now, this is my dilemma: I told her in the middle of the argument that I had bought her some traditional chocolates in my trip, but since she acted that way, I was not going to give them to her. Obviously, in the heat of the argument she said that she didn't care and that I am a resenful person. We are now ok, but I still have the chocolates in my house. Should I give them to her after all this problem? I don't want this to look like she apologized and got the chocolates as if this was a reward for her behavior.  Or should I keep them for me as a punishmente for what she did? Is that acting resentful?

author: kong88
text_post: Of course you should give them to her.  She apologized, you forgave her, right?  Don't hold onto grudges over something so small - it's petty.  You can't have a relationship that way.  Now that she's apologized, IT NEVER HAPPENED.  Don't ever mention it again or try to use this against her.
